courses.name: First Year Seminar
courses.description: Supports university transition, community connections and student planning.

courses.name: Philosophy at Northeastern
courses.description: Introduces philosophy students to liberal arts study, academic skills and the university community.

courses.name: First-Year Interdisciplinary Seminar
courses.description: Explores global citizenship, university resources and interdisciplinary problem solving.

courses.name: Professional Development for Khoury Co-op
courses.description: Prepares students for co-op applications, interviews and workplace expectations.

courses.name: Professional Development for Co-op
courses.description: Prepares students for co-op searches, interviewing, professional practice and career decisions.

courses.name: Discrete Structures
courses.description: Develops discrete structures, logic, proofs and counting methods for computing.

courses.name: Introduction to Program Design and Implementation
courses.description: Introduces programming, dataset analysis and ethical issues in software design.

courses.name: Lab for CS 2000
courses.description: Provides experiments supporting introductory programming coursework.

courses.name: Program Design and Implementation 1
courses.description: Develops program design, object-oriented abstractions and software engineering practices.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2000 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 200M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2500 with a minimum grade of D-

courses.name: Lab for CS 2100
courses.description: Provides experiments supporting program design coursework.

courses.name: Introduction to Databases
courses.description: Develops relational database design, SQL and introductory database-system techniques.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2000 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 200M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2100 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 201M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2500 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2000 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2500 with a minimum grade of D- or EECE 2560 with a minimum grade of D-

courses.name: Advanced Programming with Data
courses.description: Develops robust software architectures and data pipelines using substantial datasets.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2100 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2500 with a minimum grade of D-

courses.name: Mathematical Foundations of Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Studies the mathematical basis of AI through linear algebra, probability and computational exercises.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2100 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 201M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2510 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2500 with a minimum grade of D-

courses.name: Information Presentation and Visualization
courses.description: Studies how to design, implement and evaluate visual representations of data.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2100 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 201M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2510 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2500 with a minimum grade of D-

courses.name: Large-Scale Information Storage and Retrieval
courses.description: Studies scalable data storage, distributed databases and retrieval methods.
courses.prerequisites: ( CS 3100 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 310M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 3500 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 3500 with a minimum grade of D- ); CS 3200 with a minimum grade of D-

courses.name: Machine Learning
courses.description: Introduces predictive modeling and major supervised and unsupervised learning methods.
courses.prerequisites: DS 3000 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 250M with a minimum grade of D- or ( MATH 2331 with a minimum grade of D- ; MATH 3081 with a minimum grade of D- )

courses.name: Advanced Machine Learning
courses.description: Studies advanced learning methods and their mathematical and computational foundations.
courses.prerequisites: DS 4400 with a minimum grade of D-

courses.name: Modern Neural Networks
courses.description: Introduces neural-network training, architectures and practical applications with modern software tools.
courses.prerequisites: DS 4400 with a minimum grade of D-

courses.name: Embedded Design: Enabling Robotics
courses.description: Combines digital design, programming and embedded systems to control robotic devices.
courses.prerequisites: EECE 2140 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2510 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D-

courses.name: Fundamentals of Digital Design and Computer Organization
courses.description: Develops digital logic, computer architecture and hardware models for a simple processor.
courses.prerequisites: EECE 2160 with a minimum grade of D- or EECE 2310 with a minimum grade of D-

courses.name: Lab for EECE 2322
courses.description: Designs, simulates and tests a computer system using programmable logic.

courses.name: Digital, Analytics, Technology, and Automation Research Practicum
courses.description: Applies analytics, digital technology and machine learning to client problems through a research practicum.

courses.name: Introduction to Logic
courses.description: Develops formal logic and methods of deductive and probabilistic reasoning.

courses.name: Technology and Human Values
courses.description: Examines technology’s social dimensions and ethical implications.

courses.name: Ancient Philosophy and Political Thought
courses.description: Analyzes ancient Greek philosophy, emphasizing moral, political and metaphysical questions in Socrates, Plato and Aristotle.
courses.prerequisites: ENGL 1111 with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1111 with a minimum grade of C or WRIT 201M with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1113 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1114 with a minimum grade of C

courses.name: Ancient Philosophy and Political Thought
courses.description: Analyzes ancient Greek philosophy, emphasizing moral, political and metaphysical questions in Socrates, Plato and Aristotle.
courses.prerequisites: ENGL 1111 with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1111 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1102 with a minimum grade of C

courses.name: Modern Philosophy
courses.description: Studies early modern philosophy in historical context, including underrepresented thinkers and debates about reality, self-knowledge, injustice and human flourishing.
courses.prerequisites: ENGL 1111 with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1111 with a minimum grade of C or WRIT 201M with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1113 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1114 with a minimum grade of C; Additional course-description condition: one philosophy course.

courses.name: Advanced Deductive Logic
courses.description: Develops first-order logic, proof methods and foundational metatheory.
courses.prerequisites: MATH 1215 with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 1365 with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 298M with a minimum grade of D- or PHIL 1115 with a minimum grade of D- or PHIL 109M with a minimum grade of D-

courses.name: Advanced Inductive Logic
courses.description: Studies inductive inference, Bayesian belief revision and rational decision making.
courses.prerequisites: PHIL 1115 with a minimum grade of D- or PHIL 109M with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 1215 with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 1365 with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 298M with a minimum grade of D-

courses.name: Introduction to African American and Africana Studies
courses.description: Introduces the interdisciplinary field of African American and Africana studies and possible areas of further study.

courses.name: Goddesses, Witches, Saints, and Sinners: Women and Religion
courses.description: Examines scholarship on goddess-centered traditions and religious patriarchy through ancient images, rituals, scripture and other texts.

courses.name: Sex in Judaism, Christianity, and Islam
courses.description: Compares Jewish, Christian and Islamic approaches to gender, sexuality, marriage and family life in historical and contemporary contexts.

courses.name: Human Rights
courses.description: Examines the foundations, institutions and contemporary disputes of human rights, including genocide, refugee protection and torture.

courses.name: Possession, Sacrifice, and Divination in African Diasporic Religions
courses.description: Compares African and diasporic religious traditions, emphasizing transformations associated with enslavement and forced migration.

courses.name: Race and Religion in Film
courses.description: Critically analyzes film portrayals of African and diasporic identities, religion and intersecting systems of social power.

courses.name: Indigenous Philosophy
courses.description: Studies diverse Indigenous philosophical traditions through prose, poetry and film, addressing sovereignty, environmental justice, gender and decolonization.
courses.prerequisites: Additional course-description condition: two philosophy and/or religious studies courses.

courses.name: Religion, Race, and Politics
courses.description: Examines religion, race and political power through historical and ethnographic perspectives on social hierarchy and change.

courses.name: Philosophy of Race and Racism
courses.description: Uses philosophical analysis to examine race, racism, intersecting oppression and proposals for addressing racial injustice.
courses.prerequisites: Additional course-description condition: Registration requires two prior courses in philosophy or department permission.

courses.name: Information and Uncertainty
courses.description: Develops probabilistic inference and information theory for reasoning under uncertainty.

courses.name: Knowledge in a Digital World
courses.description: Examines digital technology’s effects on knowledge through ethics and epistemology.

courses.name: Ethics and Evolutionary Games
courses.description: Applies evolutionary game theory to the emergence and persistence of cooperation, fairness, altruism and social norms.

courses.name: Information Ethics
courses.description: Examines justice, rights and ethical responsibilities in information technologies.
courses.prerequisites: PHIL 1145 with a minimum grade of D- or PHIL 1300 with a minimum grade of D- or IS 1300 with a minimum grade of D- or graduate program admission

courses.name: Artificial Intelligence and Society
courses.description: Examines AI’s societal effects and approaches to aligning technologies with ethical values.

courses.name: AI Ethics
courses.description: Examines AI ethics, including fairness, responsibility, privacy and effects on work.
courses.prerequisites: PHIL 1145 with a minimum grade of D- or PHIL 1300 with a minimum grade of D- or IS 1300 with a minimum grade of D- or graduate program admission

courses.name: Calculus 1 for Science and Engineering
courses.description: Develops differentiation, its scientific applications, and introductory integration.

courses.name: Statistics for Economists
courses.description: Applies statistical inference, regression and data visualization to economic and social questions.
courses.prerequisites: (CS 1100 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2000 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 200M (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2100 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 201M (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2500 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2000 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2500 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or MISM 2510 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- )

courses.name: First-Year Writing
courses.description: Develops research and writing across audiences and genres through workshop practice.

courses.name: Advanced Writing in the Technical Professions
courses.description: Develops research and communication in technical and professional genres.
courses.prerequisites: ENGW 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1111 with a minimum grade of C or WRIT 201M with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1111 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1113 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1114 with a minimum grade of C

courses.name: Advanced Writing in the Humanities
courses.description: Develops interpretive argument and textual evidence in humanities writing.
courses.prerequisites: ENGW 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1111 with a minimum grade of C or WRIT 201M with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1111 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1113 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1114 with a minimum grade of C

courses.name: Interdisciplinary Advanced Writing in the Disciplines
courses.description: Develops research, revision and writing across disciplinary contexts.
courses.prerequisites: ENGW 1111 with a minimum grade of C or WRIT 201M with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1111 with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1113 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1114 with a minimum grade of C

notes: Credits use the catalog’s stated semester hours. Bundle credits belong to requirement nodes; individual amounts are supplied only when independently stated by a course catalog. Unverified alternative-course amounts and variable-credit scalar amounts remain unknown.
Course categories are editorial taxonomy. Outcomes summarize explicit program-overview statements; they are not measured graduate outcomes.
All major-page tables and policy references are represented. Partial status does not imply that the universitywide degree curriculum is complete.

Universitywide and NUpath criteria are now represented through verified shared policy bindings. The major-page reference notes describe what that page incorporates; linked policy rules appear separately in the resolved graph.

Open subject/level ranges, explicit grade/overlap limits and advisor-approved substitutions are represented criteria, not missing invented finite course lists. Individual approvals and registration eligibility remain governed by those rules.

NUpath is competency-based: approved attributes may be met through major or elective courses. This inventory does not fabricate all eligible class sections. BA-language, NYC-campus and nursing-specific general-education panels are not inherited by these Boston BS/BSEnvE degrees.
